The four questions

A session is a real process, but no single field tells you its whole story. Ask four separate questions to learn whether it is alive, what it said, what it was told, and what tm8 commands it ran.

02Attach: observe or own the terminal

    
session attach opens the live PTY stream. Choose view to observe; choose drive to own terminal input. The mode is part of a short-lived stream grant.

    

      

        

          
          
        

        

          MVMara
          
          observes PTY
        

        
View receives terminal output without terminal ownership.

        
Drive is gated.In v1, drive input is granted only to the spawning owner. A spawned session cannot use drive to contact another session.

      

      

        

          
tm8 — northlake — stream grantgrant only

          



        

        
--format json implies --grant-only: interactive terminal bytes are not DTO output. The example token is fictional and shortened.

      

    

  


  

    
03Read each answer honestly

    

      
Liveness is not status
It says which sessions have a live PTY on this server process right now. nodeBootId changes on restart; compare snapshots only within one boot.

      
Transcript is not the terminal
It reads the agent’s native transcript. Tool names may appear; tool arguments and outputs never do. stuck is a heuristic, not a liveness signal.

      
Launch is recorded bytes
Prompts are read from storage, not recomposed. Environment variable names are returned; values are structurally absent. Older sessions may answer not_recorded.

      
Journal is not token spend
It records only tm8 commands, not shell history. Token counts are chars/4 estimates of CLI-bound text, not provider usage or session spend.
